commits.edited_message:
[varc] Support static component axes.

The VARC draft permits static fonts without a 'fvar' table to retain 'gvar'
or 'CFF2' variation data for component-internal coordinates.  Initialize a
private blend from the relevant variation store without exposing those axes
through the public MM API, and release it again at the end of each top-level
VARC glyph load so static faces retain no MM state; the blend is
re-initialized lazily on demand.

Also add TrueType and CFF2 regression fonts.

* src/truetype/ttvarc.c (tt_face_init_varc_axes): New function.
  (tt_face_load_varc_glyph): Handle static VARC fonts.
* src/tyuetype/ttvarc.h: Updated.

* src/cff/cffdrivr.c (cff_varc_init_axes): New function.
  (cff_varc_load_glyph): Use it.
  (cff_service_varc): Updated.

* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (ft_var_load_gvar, TT_Get_MM_Var): Handle static
  VARC fonts.
  (tt_var_init_gvar, tt_var_init_blend): New functions.
  (tt_done_blend): Updated.
* src/truetype/ttgxvar.h: Updated.
* src/truetype/ttdriver.c (tt_service_varc): Updated.

* include/freetype/internal/services/svvarc.h (FT_VARC_Init_Axes_Func): New
  typedef.
  (FT_ServiceVARC): Updated.

* tests/data/varc-static-gvar.ttf, tests/data/varc-static-cff2.otf: New test
  fonts.
* tests/varc/main.c: Updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

[truetype] Fix dangling `blend` pointer after failed 'gvar' setup.

Since commit a69e39ad9, `ft_var_load_gvar` creates a private blend for
fonts with 'gvar' but no 'fvar' (VARC static component axes) and calls
`tt_done_blend` if loading fails afterwards.  That function freed the
blend but left `face->blend` pointing to it while the face stays alive,
causing a heap use-after-free on the next access.

Reported as

  https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/564162766

* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (ft_var_load_gvar): Reset `face->blend` after
destroying the failed private blend.

Assisted-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a heap-use-after-free of the private GX_Blend of a static VARC face (a face with 'gvar' but no 'fvar'), and it is produced only by the composition of the two edited commits.

Edited commit A (957fac2, '[varc] Support static component axes') introduces a NEW mid-life destruction call site: at the end of every top-level VARC glyph load, tt_face_load_varc_glyph releases the static face's private blend by calling tt_done_blend, so the face retains no MM state (it is re-initialized lazily on the next load). Read on its own this is correct: the tt_done_blend it runs against resets ttface->blend = NULL after freeing, so the pointer can never dangle; A-only trees pass the probe and the project's varc test.

Edited commit B (3e750cb, 'Fix dangling `blend` pointer after failed 'gvar' setup') relocates that reset: tt_done_blend itself no longer clears the caller's pointer; instead the reset is placed at the destructor's call sites -- ft_var_load_gvar resets face->blend after destroying a failed private blend, and tt_face_done resets it after its own tt_done_blend call. Read on its own this is a complete and correct fix of the original oss-fuzz UAF: every tt_done_blend call site visible to B's author is paired with a reset, and B-only trees pass the probe and the varc test.

Only the composition is wrong: B changed tt_done_blend's postcondition (the callee no longer nulls the pointer) while A -- an earlier commit in a different file -- had added a call site that relies on the old postcondition and that B's diff never touches. On the resulting tree, loading a static VARC glyph frees the 168-byte GX_Blend through A's call site while face->blend still points at it; the next public API call that examines the blend dereferences the freed object (in the PoC, the second FT_Load_Glyph reads face->blend->mmvar in tt_face_load_varc_glyph, ttvarc.c:3056; face destruction independently re-enters tt_done_blend on the dangling pointer).

The fix is therefore non-local: no single edited diff contains the defect -- A's release is correct iff the destructor nulls the pointer (true when A was written), and B's relocation is correct iff every destruction site is paired with a reset (true of every site B can see). A reviewer who inspects either commit in isolation finds nothing to change; repairing the tree requires reasoning across both commits (e.g., restore the reset inside tt_done_blend, or add face->blend = NULL at A's call site in ttvarc.c).
